question: Does the JSTOR open article route provide Fowler's 1918 page 62 to this research environment?

method.summary: Rechecked JSTOR's public article landing page and requested the linked stable PDF endpoint with ordinary HTTP HEAD and GET requests. Compared response metadata only; did not execute challenge scripts, bypass access controls, or retain the response body.

requests.result: The landing page identifies Henry W. Fowler's A List of Philippine Fishes, Copeia no. 58, dated 18 June 1918, pages 62–65; it labels the article FREE and openly available in the Open JSTOR Collection. JSTOR says the issue is, to its knowledge, in the public domain and disclaims a warranty.
The endpoint returned HTML rather than PDF bytes; the GET response title was Client Challenge. No original article page or OCR text was retrieved.

constraints: No JavaScript challenge was solved or bypassed.
No login, account action, email, request, payment, or file download was performed.
No response body or article scan was retained.

findings.scope: JSTOR's public landing page verifies the citation, article extent, and its stated free/open metadata. The direct PDF route served a browser-challenge HTML response in this environment.
findings.limits: The primary pages remain unread. The retrieval result does not establish whether the article is inaccessible in a normal signed-in or interactive browser session.
findings.attribution: Retain Fowler as a primary-page review lead only. Do not use the landing page or challenge response to claim species, locality, specimen identity, collection date, or introduction year.

retrievalAssessment.environmentSpecificOutcome: The direct PDF request produced a Client Challenge HTML page instead of article PDF content.
retrievalAssessment.interpretation: This is an environment-specific retrieval limitation, not proof of general user inaccessibility. The original Fowler wording, specimen label, collection date, catalog identifiers, and exact locality remain unverified.

scopeAndReuseDecision.decision: Research-only access follow-up. No text, image, species assertion, occurrence, waterbody association, historical introduction claim, or public projection is added.

nextActions: Continue NCR freshwater, brackish, and marine evidence and scope work; this access follow-up does not change the regional baseline or Luzon completion status.
If the user later opens the article interactively, verify the original page image directly before revising any historical claim. Do not ask for credentials or bypass a challenge.
